description: traingraph is a bundle of tools for extracting railway data from an OpenStreetMap dump and loading it into a PostgreSQL and PostGIS database as an abstract graph of nodes and edges. Step-by-step instructions build the database, Python scripts assemble paths and line strings, and a route finder returns the shortest path between two stations or coordinates as KML; the README points to a SQL dump built this way for the whole European rail network. It was written by the trainhack community on GitHub. Coverage: any area in the OSM dump; the prepared dump covers Europe. Access: source on GitHub; licence and cost: free to read, with no licence file found, so reuse terms are unclear. Caveats, stated in the README: stations are not graph nodes, so points within 80 m are patched in; depots, sidings and double tracks remain as separate edges; and the shortest path may not be a path a train could run, such as reversing at a Y junction. The code is old and unmaintained. It prepares rail network topology for network flow and cascading failure studies and builds on the OpenStreetMap and OpenRailwayMap data catalogued here.
